name: Getty Center
records_note: Parent J. Paul Getty Trust posts audited financial statements for 2008 to 2025 and lists its trustees; no annual report or donor list found.

name: Glenbow
watch: Chevron Canada and Power Corp on donor roll.
why_flagged: Chevron Canada and Power Corp on donor roll.
records_note: Glenbow posts yearly reports and financial statements from 2016-17 to 2025-26, a named donor list to March 2025, and its 19-member board.

name: Golden Thread Gallery
funding: £400k income (FY2025); Arts Council NI, National Lottery, Belfast City Council, Art Fund, Gulbenkian, Ireland Funds, Ampersand, Future Screens NI.
watch: The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, a current funder, is endowed by an oil fortune and held oil firm Partex until 2019; protesters objected in 2016.
why_flagged: £400k income (FY2025); Arts Council NI, National Lottery, Belfast City Council, Art Fund, Gulbenkian, Ireland Funds, Ampersand, Future Screens NI.
records_note: Shows funder logos with no names or date, and posts no annual reports, accounts or board; the company is on the Northern Ireland register.

name: Goldsmiths CCA
watch: Removed Gertler donor names after a 2024 occupation.
why_flagged: Removed Gertler donor names after a 2024 occupation.
records_note: It has none of its own; parent Goldsmiths, University of London posts annual reports from 2019 and lists its Council. The CCA names donors undated.

name: Govett-Brewster / Len Lye Centre
watch: Todd Energy, an oil and gas producer, is founding partner.
why_flagged: Todd Energy, an oil and gas producer, is founding partner.
records_note: The gallery has no reports of its own; owner New Plymouth District Council posts audited annual reports for 2013 to 2025. Partners show as logos.

name: Grand People's Study House
watch: North Korea's Library Law treats libraries as essential for promoting ideology. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: State library and Juche study centre: 100,000 m², 600 rooms, claimed capacity 30 million books. A 1989 broadcast claimed over 10 million visits a year; budget unpublished.
records_note: Its official site, gpsh.edu.kp, does not resolve from outside North Korea, so no records could be checked.

name: Greenland National Museum and Archives (Nunatta Katersugaasivia Allagaateqarfialu)
watch: Excluded funder is current. The 2024 annual report records a DKK 4.5M grant from Augustinus Fonden (a Scandinavian Tobacco Group holder) for the 3-year Angerlartunnguit research project on the Uunartoq Thule Inuit. It also records a DKK 300,000 Augustinus grant for the PoTraCh airport documentation and Augustinus co-funding of the Qimmit project (2023-26).

name: Groninger Museum
watch: GasTerra and Gasunie funding; Fossil Free Culture actions 2025 and 2026.
why_flagged: GasTerra and Gasunie funding; Fossil Free Culture actions 2025 and 2026.
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2005 to 2024 with a financial section, names GasTerra and Gasunie among sponsors, and names its supervisory board.

name: Guggenheim Abu Dhabi
funding: Owned by Abu Dhabi's state-owned Tourism Development and Investment Company; the Guggenheim Foundation runs the programme. The Department of Culture and Tourism set the opening for 11 December 2026.
watch: Gulf Labor Coalition has campaigned for about 16 years, staged a 2014 protest at the New York Guggenheim and called for an artist boycott.
why_flagged: Owned by Abu Dhabi's state-owned Tourism Development and Investment Company; the Guggenheim Foundation runs the programme. The Department of Culture and Tourism set the opening for 11 December 2026.
records_note: Its site refused every page fetch, so reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked; the project is run with Abu Dhabi's culture department.

name: Guggenheim Bilbao
watch: Petronor refinery sits on the board.
why_flagged: Petronor refinery sits on the board.
records_note: It posts the 2025 activity report and 2025 accounts for three entities, and lists corporate members by name; trustees show only as organisations.

name: Gwangju Biennale
watch: The Park Seo-Bo Prize was abolished in 2023 after one edition, following public protest.
why_flagged: Public funding and related spending top 10 billion won per edition; the 2026 operating budget is about 14.3 billion won. Park Seo-Bo's GIZI Foundation funded a prize until 2023.
records_note: The foundation lists its trustees and auditors by name, posts audited financial statements (2020 and 2021 seen), and shows past sponsors as logos.

name: Haifa Museum of Art
funding: Municipal museum group Haifa Museums. Site logos: Haifa Municipality, Ministry of Culture and Sport, Mizrahi Tefahot bank. Japan's embassy gave NIS 15,620 for a 2025 Tikotin show.
watch: In January 2019 hundreds protested the loaned McJesus sculpture. Minister Regev threatened to defund the museum; a deputy attorney general rebuked her. It was removed.
why_flagged: Municipal museum group Haifa Museums. Site logos: Haifa Municipality, Ministry of Culture and Sport, Mizrahi Tefahot bank. Japan's embassy gave NIS 15,620 for a 2025 Tikotin show.
records_note: No reports or accounts; the sponsorship page names one 2025 foreign-state donor, the Embassy of Japan, beside logos, and the board of directors is listed.
